title: The money path is simulated by default: offer/onboarding/nudge emails terminate in the local outbox, addressed to a NAME not an address, and detached links are host-less without APP_BASE_URL
expected: Extending an offer results in the candidate actually receiving the tokenized link (real delivery, or an explicit in-product step handing the recruiter the link to deliver).
got: sendComm defaults to OutboxChannel with terminal status 'queued' (comms.ts:36-42) unless COMMS_WEBHOOK_URL is set; the recipient contract resolves to candidateLabel (a display name) for any non-inbound entry (comms-dispatch.ts:49-68), which a relay dead-letters; heartbeat/accept-time links are built from publicBaseUrl() with no request origin, yielding host-less paths when APP_BASE_URL/NEXT_PUBLIC_APP_BASE_URL is unset (public-base-url.ts:30-42, comms-dispatch.ts:431-433, offer-reminders.ts:30-31, preboarding-reminders.ts:33).
ceiling: Real delivery requires three env prerequisites at once (COMMS_WEBHOOK_URL relay, APP_BASE_URL/NEXT_PUBLIC_APP_BASE_URL, and a captured deliverable contact — only inbound applicants have one). Out of the box the offer never leaves the machine; the Outbox is an honest audit log, not a mailbox. Severity already dropped one level (blocker→major) per the demo-scope rule; the design is documented in docs/COMMS_DELIVERY.md.
scope_note: Also hits Petra: nothing on the Decisions/Pipeline surfaces distinguishes 'queued locally' from 'delivered' at the moment of send (the Comms Center shows it one tab away).
suggested_acceptance: With a relay + base URL configured and an inbound-applicant entry, extending an offer produces an outbox row with status 'sent' whose body contains an ABSOLUTE /offer/[token] link; keyless/relayless, the send surface itself tells the recruiter the message is queued locally and offers the link to copy.
l2_priority: Extend a real offer keyless: confirm the outbox row (kind 'offer', status 'queued') carries the link, confirm whether the link is absolute or host-less, and walk the only manual delivery path (Comms Center expand → copy). If a relay is available, verify envelope delivery end-to-end.

title: Silent success on 'Send offer': the Decisions card fades out and the returned { offerExtended, link } is discarded — no confirmation of what was sent, to whom, until when, and no offer-link panel anywhere
expected: After the send click, an explicit confirmation ('Offer sent to <name>, valid until <date>') plus the tokenized link for manual delivery — matching the TokenLinkPanel pattern the drawer already has for voice and scheduling links.
got: DecisionsTab.act() removes the card after 260 ms and only checks r.ok, discarding the response payload (DecisionsTab.tsx:176-214) even though the route returns { offerExtended: true, link } (route.ts:76). CandidateDrawer mounts TokenLinkPanels for voice and scheduling but none for the live offer token (CandidateDrawer.tsx:88-89,818,882). The link is retrievable only from the Comms Center outbox body (CommsCenter.tsx:261).
scope_note: Shared with tomas-hiring-manager — it is his 'unambiguous confirmation of what he just decided' criterion; both characters hit it on every single offer.
suggested_acceptance: Clicking 'Send offer' surfaces a confirmation containing the candidate name, the deadline date, and the copyable /offer/[token] link (or a one-click path to it).
l2_priority: Live: approve an offer in Decisions and record exactly what feedback appears (or doesn't) after the click; verify the only link-recovery path is the Comms Center.

title: Offer-letter language is guessed from CV languages while the email chrome localizes by the entry's stored locale — a mixed-language offer email is structurally possible
expected: One language authority for the whole offer email: the candidate's stored locale (captured at apply) drives both the LLM letter and the deterministic footer.
got: draft_offer picks Czech only if the CV's languages blob contains 'czech/česk' (automation.py:110-112,727), while dispatchOffer's fallback subject + response footer localize via entry.locale (comms-dispatch.ts:239-245, NULL⇒'en' for recruiter/Match-sourced entries). A cs-locale candidate whose CV omits Czech gets an English letter over a Czech footer (and vice versa).
scope_note: Shared with petra-recruiter (English-only headline output is her declared finding; robotic/mixed comms is Tereza's). Frequency 'med': ČS-corpus candidates usually list Czech, but Match-sourced entries default locale to 'en'.
suggested_acceptance: The offer task receives the entry's locale (like prep's --lang, automation-run.ts:172) and the letter + footer render in the same language.
l2_priority: Generate a real offer for a cs-locale entry whose profile languages lack 'Czech' and read the actual outbox body: assert letter and footer languages match.

title: The offer letter is below the senior offer-comm bar: no decision deadline, no start date, no benefits, no named contact — grounding 4/8 on the journey's one AI surface
expected: An offer email a senior recruiter would send: figure + basis, the validity deadline (it exists — it's the product's own lever), start-date/next-step expectations, and a human sender.
got: The prompt feeds only candidate label, role, company, figure and guessed language (automation.py:733-737); ttlDays is chosen AFTER the draft at approval time (AiReviewCard.tsx:21, route.ts:50) and never enters the letter — the dispatch footer appends only the link (comms-dispatch.ts:241-243). The candidate learns the deadline only by opening the page (page.tsx:267-280) or from the T-48h nudge (comms.offerReminder does state it).
scope_note: Grounding audit: identity ✓, role+company ✓, real band ✓, fit-scaled figure with basis ✓; language ✗ (wrong source, OO-L1-03), CV evidence ✗, terms beyond salary ✗, deadline ✗ → 4/8. Terms like start date/benefits also have no data model to draw from — part missing-feature, not only prompt-thinness.
suggested_acceptance: The dispatched offer email states the response deadline; the letter references at least one candidate-specific fact and the terms the deployment can supply.
l2_priority: Read the real dispatched letter body (LLM path, keys present): score it against the senior bar — does it state the deadline, anything beyond the salary line, anything specific to this candidate?

title: Offer expiry is a silent terminal transition for the candidate: the lapse records internal events only — no comm is dispatched when the offer dies
expected: Per Tereza's scored criterion, every transition produces a message: an expiry notice ('your offer lapsed on <date>; contact us if you still want to talk') mirrors the rejection comm.
got: lapseExpiredOffers / expireOfferIfDue record an 'offer_expired' automation event for the recruiter's timeline but call no dispatcher (offers-store.ts:171-206); the heartbeat sweep only logs the count (instrumentation-node.ts:69-78). The only pre-warning is the single T-48h nudge (offer-reminders.ts:19-46), itself delivery-dependent. The candidate discovers expiry only by opening the dead link (page.tsx:255-261).
scope_note: Severity per the character's pre-declared criterion (silent terminal transition = major); computed impact is tempered by low frequency (only unanswered offers) and the existing T-48h nudge.
suggested_acceptance: When an offer lapses, a localized expiry comm is queued to the candidate (same channel + GDPR footer as every other transition comm).
l2_priority: Mint a 1-day-TTL offer, let it lapse via the sweep, and confirm no candidate-facing outbox row appears at expiry (only the internal event).

title: Drawer timeline renders an expired offer as 'Offer extended' twice — the timeline emits status 'expired' but the row renderer has no offerExpired label
expected: An expired offer reads 'Offer expired' at its deadline on the candidate timeline.
got: candidate-timeline.ts deliberately pushes a second item {kind:'offer', status:'expired'} at expiresAt 'so it doesn't render as extended forever' (candidate-timeline.ts:72-76), but TimelineItemRow maps any non-accepted/declined status to t('offerExtended') (CandidateDrawer.tsx:939-940) and messages/cs.json pipeline.drawer.timeline has no offerExpired key — so the recruiter sees 'Nabídka odeslána' twice.
suggested_acceptance: The timeline row for status 'expired' renders a distinct localized 'offer expired' label in both catalogs.
l2_priority: After the OO-L1-05 lapse scenario, open the candidate drawer and screenshot the duplicated 'extended' rows.

title: The Decisions approval card sends a letter the approver never sees: subject/body exist in the approval payload but the card renders only number, band, rationale and deadline
expected: The 'Send offer' card offers at least a collapsible preview of the letter that will go out in the company's name.
got: AiReviewCard renders parsed.recommended/salaryMin/salaryMax/rationale + the ttl input (AiReviewCard.tsx:55-100) but never parsed.subject/parsed.body, which are present in approvalDetail (automation.py:767-778 result fields; drawer's own result view shows them at CandidateResultView.tsx:108-109). The approve click dispatches that unseen body (route.ts:72).
suggested_acceptance: The offer_review card exposes the letter (expandable) so the approver has seen what their click sends.
l2_priority: Confirm live that no path from the Decisions card shows the letter before sending.

title: Client-side deadline default reads a non-NEXT_PUBLIC env var: a deployment's KP_OFFER_TTL_DAYS never reaches the AiReviewCard input, which always shows 7
expected: The UI default deadline mirrors the deployment default.
got: defaultOfferTtlDays() reads process.env.KP_OFFER_TTL_DAYS (offer-policy.ts:21-24); in the 'use client' AiReviewCard (AiReviewCard.tsx:7,21) Next.js only inlines NEXT_PUBLIC_ vars, so the browser value is always the 7-day fallback. Behavior stays consistent (the displayed value is what's sent, route.ts:50) but a configured deployment default silently never applies to UI-extended offers.
suggested_acceptance: The card's initial ttl value comes from a server-provided default (or a NEXT_PUBLIC mirror), not a client env read.

title: Custom pre-boarding questionnaire fields render their recruiter-authored labels to the candidate — only the six default keys localize
expected: A Czech candidate sees the whole questionnaire in Czech.
got: The candidate page localizes only the FIELD_LABEL default keys and falls back to the authored label for custom/preset fields (onboarding/[token]/page.tsx:21-28,110-111; onboarding.ts:28-40 documents this). A template authored in English yields mixed-language fields on a cs candidate's page.
ceiling: Custom fields are free-text data, not catalog keys — they render in whatever language the recruiter authored; only the default six are translatable. A ČS tenant authoring templates in Czech avoids it in practice.
suggested_acceptance: Either per-locale labels on custom fields, or a lint that warns when a template's field language differs from the tenant's candidate locale.

title: STRENGTH — accept lands on a concrete onboarding next step, tripled-up: inline CTA on the accepted card, welcome-email footer, and a lazily-ensured run so the link works even if the accept-time hook failed
expected: The journey's crux: no dead-end 'People will be in touch'.
got: Accepted card links /onboarding/${offer.token} inline (page.tsx:239-248); dispatchOnboarding appends the same link (offer-finalize.ts:109-111, comms-dispatch.ts:431-433); startRun is idempotent at accept (offer-finalize.ts:97-107) AND the resolver re-ensures it (onboarding-candidate.ts:21-22). One token serves both legs; a non-accepted token 404s, leaking nothing (onboarding-candidate.ts:17-24).
ceiling: The next step is a questionnaire + progress reassurance, not the full onboarding (contract e-sign is a provider seam, onboarding.ts:1-6; not eIDAS-compliant in-app).
suggested_acceptance: Keep: L2 should confirm the accepted card's CTA opens a populated questionnaire with the same token.
l2_priority: Accept a real offer token and follow the inline CTA — confirm the questionnaire renders populated and submits.

title: STRENGTH — the candidate's decision is protected in both directions: deliberate decline (alertdialog, safe focus), ambiguous-POST reconcile, 410-distinct expiry, and a stale decline can never demote a Hired candidate
got: Inline confirm with focus moved to 'Go back' (page.tsx:48-56,290-331); reconcile re-reads authoritative status after a dropped POST (page.tsx:105-118); expired is its own 410 → definite card, not a retry loop (route.ts:32-34, page.tsx:132-135,255-261); markEntryStatus refuses to overwrite terminal/Hired entries and logs the blocked write (offers-store.ts:303-336).
ceiling: Decline is terminal with no 'changed my mind' path — reversal requires the recruiter re-extending a new offer.
suggested_acceptance: Keep; do not add friction to accept.

title: STRENGTH — offer lifecycle concurrency is production-grade: one open offer per entry (partial unique index + immediate transaction), CAS single-claimer terminal side effects, idempotent re-extends resend the SAME link
expected: Double-clicks and concurrent actors must not mint duplicate live offers or double-fire Hired/onboarding.
got: uq_offers_open_entry partial index (offers-store.ts:67-71) + getOrCreateOpenOffer tx.immediate (offers-store.ts:268-276); markOfferResponded CAS with the claimer alone running side effects (offers-store.ts:284-298, offer-finalize.ts:41-59); a comms blip on accept records a durable onboarding_failed reconcile event instead of 500ing a committed accept (offer-finalize.ts:112-123).
ceiling: Legacy DBs already holding duplicate open offers skip the index creation (logged) until an operator cleans up (offers-store.ts:66-71).

title: STRENGTH — the per-offer deadline lever (commit b7c40a8) is wired end-to-end: Decisions input (1–90d) → mint-time stamp → candidate countdown (coral <48h) → at-most-once T-48h nudge → lazy + swept lapse with audit events
expected: A deadline that actually forces a timely decision and frees headcount.
got: AiReviewCard ttl input (AiReviewCard.tsx:85-100) → route ttlDays (route.ts:50) → validated resolveOfferTtlMs + expires_at at mint (offer-policy.ts:32-36, offers-store.ts:133-135) → page countdown (page.tsx:267-280) → CAS-claimed reminder (offers-store.ts:213-241, offer-reminders.ts:19-46) → expireOfferIfDue on read/respond + heartbeat sweep, both recording offer_expired (offers-store.ts:171-206, instrumentation-node.ts:69-89). Sweeps run unconditionally on the heartbeat, independent of the opt-in policy scheduler.
ceiling: Legacy null-deadline offers never expire (fail-open, offer-policy.ts:58-63); the nudge is at-most-once and not retried on dispatch failure; delivery itself is OO-L1-01's seam.
suggested_acceptance: Keep: L2 confirms the countdown renders the seeded deadline and turns coral inside 48h.
l2_priority: Verify the live countdown against a minted short-TTL offer in cs locale (date formatting via Intl, page.tsx:272-274).

title: STRENGTH — the pre-boarding questionnaire is a visible, nudged loop (commit 3c9f4f8): pending/done chip on every run card, answers pre-fill the run detail, submission stamps the timeline, and one deliverability-checked nudge fires on the heartbeat
expected: A hire who never fills the questionnaire must be visible, not a silently-empty record.
got: intakeSubmitted chip (OnboardingTab.tsx:163-171, onboarding-store.ts:247-261); duePreboardingReminders + CAS claim AFTER entry/link resolution so an undeliverable run doesn't burn its one shot (onboarding-store.ts:266-289, preboarding-reminders.ts:20-48); intake mirrored to the recruiter timeline (onboarding-candidate.ts:64-67); answers pre-filled in RunDetailView (OnboardingTab.tsx:385,467-485).
ceiling: One nudge total, and it needs an accepted-offer token to link to (manual hires without an offer can't be nudged, preboarding-reminders.ts:28-29); nudge delivery rides the OO-L1-01 channel.
suggested_acceptance: Keep: L2 confirms submitted answers appear on the recruiter's run detail and the chip flips to done.
l2_priority: Submit the questionnaire as the candidate and verify the chip + answers on the Onboarding tab.

title: STRENGTH — Hired is protected as an outcome-bearing terminal: a manual stage move to Hired is 422-refused and routed through the offer flow, so every hire has an offer record, an acceptance, and an onboarding hand-off
expected: No 'hire' can exist without its decision trail.
got: set_stage → Hired returns 422 with an instructive message (route.ts:96-107); the only path to Hired is the candidate's accept (offer-finalize.ts:57-66), which also seals the outcome + fires onboarding + mirrors to a configured ATS (offer-finalize.ts:79-129).
ceiling: A genuinely out-of-band hire (walk-in, referral signed on paper) has no expressible path except minting a pro-forma offer and accepting it on the candidate's behalf.
suggested_acceptance: Keep; verify the 422 message guides the recruiter to 'move to Offer → extend'.
